---
title: "7. Your first AmberMakie plot"
subtitle: "Turn a transient result into an inspectable engineering figure"
julia:
  env: ["JULIA_PROJECT=../../../AmberMakie/docs"]
---

```{julia}
#| include: false
using Pkg
Pkg.activate(joinpath(@__DIR__, "../../../AmberMakie/docs"))
using Amber, AmberMakie, CairoMakie
CairoMakie.activate!()
set_theme!(theme_amber_light())
```

AmberMakie plots Amber result objects directly. You select signals by their
Amber names, so the plotting code does not need to unpack columns or keep a
separate time vector in sync.

```{julia}
@circuit MakieRCStep() begin
    gnd = ground()
    input = node()
    output = node()
    Source = voltage_source(input, gnd;
        waveform=Step(low=0V, high=1V, at=100μs, rise=2μs))
    R1 = resistor(input, output; value=10kΩ)
    C1 = capacitor(output, gnd; value=10nF)
end

result = transient(MakieRCStep(), 0s => 700μs;
    saveat=2μs, max_step=2μs)

(samples=length(result.axis), converged=result.stats[:converged])
```

## Plot more than one signal

`traceplot` labels the axes with engineering units and returns a `PlotHandle`.
The handle retains the axes, plots, and semantic views if you want to customize
the figure later.

```{julia}
figure = Figure(size=(900, 520))
trace = traceplot(figure[1, 1], result; signals=[:input, :output])
Label(figure[0, 1], "10 kΩ / 10 nF step response"; fontsize=20)
figure
```

## Read the data, not the pixels

Cursor helpers snap to the original samples. This makes measurements
reproducible even when the image is resized for the web page.

```{julia}
output_view = traceview(result, :output)
readout = cursor_readout(output_view.axis, output_view.values, 200μs, 500μs)

(
    cursor_a=(time=readout.a.x, voltage=readout.a.y),
    cursor_b=(time=readout.b.x, voltage=readout.b.y),
    delta_time=readout.delta_x,
    delta_voltage=readout.delta_y,
)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
Use `workbench(result; signals=[:input, :output])` in an interactive Julia
session for linked A/B cursors and interval measurements. A static tutorial
uses `traceplot` so the rendered page remains portable.
:::
